name: FallenUnggoyRules
source:
The following are the 10 cardinal rules of the Order of the Fallen Unggoy. 
 note: any and all deviation from these rules will result in immediate jettison from your respective squad via methane tank ignition. 
 
 1: no unggoy shall refer to a fellow member or themself as `` grunt'' this demeans us as men, and as a species in general. 
 
 2: the use of infusion is strictly prohibited. 
 
 3: all unggoy shall show honor and respect to the warriors of the sangeli people, even as enemies. jiralhanae however, shall never receive such treatment. `` note: disobeying part two of this rule is permitted, but only when in the direct presence, and in danger of dismemberment by jiralhanae.'' 
 
 4: plasma grenade suicide hugs `` while appreciated'' are not a requirement. 
 
 5: never attempt a plasma grenade suicide hug while within the blast radius of your fellow unggoy 
 
 6: never attempt to fight the demon alone 
 
 7: please do not attempt to prank your fellow unggoy by jettisoning them with their methane tank, this can and will cause bodily, property, and emotional damage to all parties involved. 
 
 8: always remeber. plasma pistols take time to charge. 
 
 9: `` plasma cannon bounces'' are strictly prohibited. 
 
 10: when in doubt. flee. 
 
 by following these 10 simple rules you can and will become a valuable member of the Order of the Fallen Unggoy.
retelling:
Narrator (Demon):

In the far reaches of space, amidst the chaos and violence of an unending conflict, I found myself serving under a unique order - the Order of the Fallen Unggoy. These were not ordinary Grunts; they had chosen a path, a purpose that set them apart from their brethren.

Every day, we adhered to ten ironclad rules handed down by our enigmatic leaders. The first rule was simple: We were not to be addressed as 'grunt.' It was a reminder of the dignity we held, despite our species' reputation in this war-torn universe.

The second rule forbade us from indulging in infusion, a substance that could cloud our judgment and endanger our mission. The third mandated respect for the Sangheili, allies who fought alongside us with unwavering loyalty. Yet, we were cautioned against forming bonds with Jiralhanae, the Brutes - their volatile nature was something to be wary of, not trusted.

It was discouraged that we'd willingly risk our lives in suicidal attacks, but sometimes, when faced with no other choice, we would stand our ground against the enemy. We were taught to handle plasma grenades carefully, a lesson learned all too often by those who underestimated their power.

Solo combat was generally avoided, for the demons we fought were not to be trifled with. But when there was no other choice, we would face them head-on, using our plasma pistols as shields against their relentless onslaught. Pranks involving methane tanks were strictly prohibited; they were a precious resource, not a toy for idle amusement.

The use of plasma cannon bounces was absolutely forbidden - the resulting destruction could level entire structures and endanger our comrades. Lastly, when faced with uncertainty, we were to prioritize escape. The rules served as our lifeline in this brutal war.

Each day, I witnessed the consequences of breaking these rules. A swift ignition, a methane tank jettison, and a once fellow Unggoy was gone, expelled from our order for their transgression. It was a harsh reminder of our purpose, our commitment to this fight. We were not just soldiers; we were the Order of the Fallen Unggoy - bound by a code, forged in the fires of war.
